author: massicomar
title: Book Shop
summary:
You are in a book shop which sells $n$ different books. You know the price and number of pages of each book.

You have decided that the total price of your purchases will be at most $x$. What is the maximum number of pages you can buy? You can buy each book at most once.

Input

The first input line contains two integers $n$ and $x$: the number of books and the maximum total price.

The next line contains $n$ integers $h_1,h_2,\ldots,h_n$: the price of each book.

The last line contains $n$ integers $s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_n$: the number of pages of each book.

Output

Print one integer: the maximum number of pages.
explanation: Each book once, small budget: 0/1 knapsack over capacity. n·x = 1e8 fits with a rolled 1D array iterated downward.
traps: Iterating capacity upward in the rolled array turns it into unbounded knapsack (books reused).

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[i][c] = max pages using a subset of the first i books with total price ≤ c
dp[c] = max pages with total price ≤ c, books reusable
options.why: Books can't be bought twice; that's unbounded knapsack.

options.text: dp[mask] = pages of the chosen subset
dp[p] = minimum price to get exactly p pages
options.why: Valid idea only when total pages is small; here pages total up to 1e6 and price is the small dimension.

extraLayers.explanation: Index by the small dimension (budget ≤ 1e5) and remember which books are still available (prefix i).

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.why: Using dp[i] on the right lets book i be bought again (unbounded).

options.text: dp[c] = max over books of dp[c − price] + pages, c upward
Sort by pages/price and take greedily
options.why: Fractional-knapsack greedy is wrong for 0/1 items.

extraLayers.explanation: Book i is either skipped or bought once, using the previous row so it can't be reused.

es.explanation: Cada libro una sola vez y un presupuesto chico: mochila 0/1 sobre la capacidad. n·x = 1e8 entra con un arreglo 1D reciclado que se recorre hacia abajo.
traps: Recorrer la capacidad hacia arriba en el arreglo reciclado la convierte en mochila no acotada (libros reusados).

dp-state.explanation: Indexa por la dimensión chica (presupuesto ≤ 1e5) y recuerda qué libros siguen disponibles (el prefijo i).

why.b: Los libros no se pueden comprar dos veces; eso es mochila no acotada.
why.d: La idea sirve solo cuando el total de páginas es chico; acá las páginas suman hasta 1e6 y el precio es la dimensión chica.

dp-transition.explanation: El libro i se omite o se compra una vez, usando la fila anterior para que no se pueda reusar.

why.b: Usar dp[i] a la derecha deja comprar el libro i otra vez (no acotada).
why.d: El greedy de la mochila fraccionaria está mal para objetos 0/1.
